Subject: Request: temporary net45 + credit corridor for Q2 consumption

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re well. Quick ask from our finance team as we close Q2 — EvoThera is seeing a short timing gap on receivables and we’d like to request a temporary move from Net30 to Net45 for Redwood invoices tied to our Dedicated clusters for the next 90 days.

Couple of specifics we want to align on:
- Proposed temporary term: Net45 for Dedicated usage only (hosted API stays Net30).
- Target credit corridor: up to $250,000 to support burst capacity over the next three months.
- VAT handling: we need confirmation of the entity Redwood will invoice (EU vs US) and what evidence you require from us (VAT IDs / tax residency).

If this works, we can sign a short amendment and provide VAT certificates promptly. Appreciate a clear payment schedule or milestone ladder (e.g., phased remits or deposit) to make this operational for our AR team.

Thanks — Maria
Maria Gutierrez
CFO, EvoThera Ltd.

Maria — thanks for the clear ask and the cashflow snapshot. Looping in Laura from Finance to weigh in on credit terms.

High-level response: Redwood is open to a short-lived Net45 for Dedicated capacity, provided we put a few guardrails in place to manage exposure. Proposed guardrails that would make this acceptable to us:
- Temporary credit corridor capped at $250k, reviewed at 45 and 90 days.
- A 10% refundable security deposit applied to the corridor on activation (applied to final invoice or returned after 90 days if usage aligns).
- VAT: we will invoice the legal entity listed in your purchase order. For the EU route we need a copy of your VAT registration + proof of VAT liability (standard invoice evidence). If EvoThera wants Redwood to invoice the US entity to avoid EU VAT, we need a signed tax residency declaration.

Operational ask: I’ve attached a short amendment draft to capture these terms and a proposed remittance ladder:
- At activation: 10% security deposit (applied to credit corridor).
- Week 4: invoice as usual (Net45) for consumption; automated reminders for delinquent invoices at day 30 and day 40.
- Review points at 45 and 90 days with option to revert to Net30 if exposure is exceeded.

If that high-level approach looks acceptable, I’ll send the DocuSign amendment and loop in Billing for the setup. 

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context, Soojin and Maria. From Finance’s perspective we can agree to a trial Net45 with the following clarifications:

- Trial window: 90 days from amendment execution.
- Security deposit: 10% of the estimated quarterly run-rate (min $15k) held as refundable collateral.
- Usage monitoring: Billing will provide weekly consumption reports during the trial; if usage grows beyond the $250k corridor we’ll flag for an immediate review and either request additional collateral or reduce the credit corridor.
- VAT evidence: please upload VAT IDs and the relevant entity registration in the shared folder. For EU invoicing we require VAT certificate + company registration.

Operational next steps for smooth execution:
1) Maria: confirm preferred invoicing entity and upload VAT files (I included a checklist in the attachment).
2) Redwood: we’ll generate the DocuSign amendment and Billing will provision a temporary credit corridor in the portal.
3) Pilot: run the first 30 days under the plan with weekly usage checks — if all good, continue to day 90.

Attachment: credit-check-summary.pdf (internal summary) — this is our standard credit checklist and minimum deposit guidance.

Laid out plainly — happy to chat if you want to walk through the schedule.

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
